formula: Q = SUM over fixtures of (0.75 x V / DDT) + PD — OBC 7.4.4.3.(7)

variables.Q: flow rate through the interceptor, L/s

requirements: 7.4.4.3.(1): except in residential suites, a fixture discharging fats, oils or grease in an area where food is cooked, processed or prepared shall discharge through a grease interceptor.
7.4.4.3.(6): locate the interceptor as close as possible to the fixture(s) it serves.
7.4.4.3.(8): all grease and oil interceptors shall have an internal flow control; where head exceeds 5 ft, a secondary flow control is required.
7.2.3.2.(3)/(4): interceptors conform to CSA B481.0/B481.3 for selection and installation, and are rated to CSA B481.1 (lard) or B481.2 (oil).
CSA B481.3: a dishwasher served by an interceptor requires a dedicated grease interceptor.
CSA B481.4: service before FOG and solids exceed 25% of liquid volume, and at least once every 4 weeks.
selection: Choose a manufactured interceptor whose rated flow capacity (to CSA B481.1 or B481.2) is at least the calculated Q. Municipal guides commonly apply a 1-minute drain-down time; a 2-minute period is acceptable where conditions permit.
source: OBC 2024 Sentence 7.4.4.3.(7) formula and requirements via ontario.ca 2024 Building Code Compendium Part 7; method cross-checked against Halifax Water and City of Calgary sizing guides, verified 2026-11-15
